401909871.happened: Dallas won 113–109 in Miami. Cooper Flagg led them with 29 points, 11 assists and 6 rebounds, and P.J. Washington added 20 points and 9 rebounds. Giannis Antetokounmpo did everything he could for Miami with 29 points, 14 rebounds and 11 assists.
401909871.right: The model expected a close, low-margin game between two teams who had been losing by four to seven points a game, and it was: four points in it at the end. Naji Marshall did miss the game for Dallas, as the preview assumed.
401909871.missed: The model rated Miami clearly stronger on paper and made them a 68% favourite, and that was wrong on the night. Dallas won the rebounding battle 51–42, and Miami made only 14 of 25 free throws while Dallas made 13 of 14. That free-throw gap alone was worth more than the final margin.
401909871.why: Our team-strength rating doesn't account for a night where one side controls the boards and the other leaves points at the line. A 68% chance still means Miami lose about one game in three like this one, and this was one of them.

401909876.happened: Golden State won 134–114 in Denver. Yaxel Lendeborg scored 31 points with 12 rebounds, and Stephen Curry added 24 points, making all 3 of his three-point attempts. Golden State made 22 of 44 from three; Denver made 10 of 29.
401909876.right: Cameron Johnson didn't play for Denver, as the preview expected. Nikola Jokić still had 19 points, 7 rebounds and 11 assists.
401909876.missed: This was our biggest miss of the night. The model made Denver a 72% favourite at home, and Golden State won by 20. They made 12 more threes than Denver and out-rebounded them 45–32.
401909876.why: The model leaned on Denver's higher team-strength rating and better recent form. It has no way to see a night where one team shoots 50% from three, and Golden State's form coming in (losing by almost seven a game) didn't hint at it. We're keeping this result on the record, as we do every miss.
